title: 2022 HMMT February Guts Problem 25
statement: Let \(A B C\) be an acute scalene triangle with circumcenter \(O\) and centroid \(G\). Given that \(A G O\) is a right triangle, \(A O=9\), and \(B C=15\), let \(S\) be the sum of all possible values for the area of triangle \(A G O\). Compute \(S^{2}\).

solutions.text: Note that we know that \(O, H\), and \(G\) are collinear and that \(H G=2 O G\). Thus, let \(O G=x\) and \(H G=2 x\). We also have \(\sin A=\frac{B C}{2 R}=\frac{5}{6}\), so \(\cos A=\frac{\sqrt{11}}{6}\). Then, if \(A G \perp O G\), then we have \(x^{2}+A G^{2}=O G^{2}+A G^{2}=A O^{2}=81\) and \(H G^{2}+A G^{2}=4 x^{2}+A G^{2}=A H^{2}=(2 R \cos A)^{2}=99\). Solving gives us \(x=\sqrt{6}\) and \(A G=5 \sqrt{3}\). Thus, the area of \(A G O\) in this case is \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \sqrt{6} \cdot 5 \sqrt{3}=\frac{5 \sqrt{3}}{2}\). If we have \(A O \perp O G\), then we have \(99=A H^{2}=A O^{2}+O H^{2}=81+9 x^{2}\). This gives us \(x=\sqrt{2}\). In this case, we have the area of \(A G O\) is \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \sqrt{2} \cdot 9=\frac{9 \sqrt{2}}{2}\). Adding up the two areas gives us \(S=12 \sqrt{2}\). Squaring gives \(S^{2}=288\).
